title: Calculations using Born-Haber Cycles

blocks.md: - Once a Born-Haber cycle has been constructed, it is possible to calculate the lattice energy (Δ*H*<sub>*latt*</sub><sup>ꝋ</sup>) by applying Hess’s law and rearranging:
If we simplify this into three terms, this makes the equation easier to see:

- Δ*H*<sub>*latt*</sub><sup>θ</sup>
- Δ*H*<sub>*f*</sub><sup>θ</sup>
- Δ*H*<sub>*1*</sub><sup>θ </sup>(the sum of all of the various enthalpy changes necessary to convert the elements in their standard states to gaseous ions)
- The simplified equation becomes
So, if we rearrange to calculate the lattice energy, the equation becomes

- When calculating the Δ*H*<sub>*latt*</sub><sup>θ</sup>, all other necessary values will be given in the question
- A Born-Haber cycle could be used to calculate any stage in the cycle

  - For example, you could be given the lattice energy and asked to calculate the enthalpy change of formation of the ionic compound
  - The principle would be exactly the same
  - Work out the **direct** and **indirect route** of the cycle (the stage that you are being asked to calculate will always be the direct route)
  - Write out the equation in terms of enthalpy changes and rearrange if necessary to calculate the required value
- **Remember:** sometimes a value may need to be doubled or halved, depending on the ionic solid involved

  - For example, with MgCl<sub>2</sub> the value for the first electron affinity of chlorine would need to be doubled in the calculation, because there are two moles of chlorine atoms
  - Therefore, you are adding **2 moles** of electrons to **2 moles** of chlorine atoms, to form **2 moles** of Cl<sup>-</sup> ions

blocks.label: Worked Example
blocks.md:
Using the data below, calculate the Δ*H*<sub>latt</sub><sup>θ</sup> of potassium chloride, KCl.

|   | **Δ*****H***<sub>***at***</sub><sup>**θ **</sup>**/ kJ mol**<sup>**–1**</sup> | **IE / EA**<sup>*** ***</sup>**/ kJ mol**<sup>**–1**</sup> |
|---|---|---|
| K | +90 | +418 |
| Cl | +122 | -349 |
| **Δ*****H***<sub>***f***</sub><sup>**θ **</sup>**/ kJ mol**<sup>**–1**</sup> |   |   |
| KCl | -437 |   |

**Answer:**

- **Step 1: **The corresponding Born-Haber cycle is:

![Flowchart illustrating thermochemical cycle for KCl formation, showing direct and indirect routes, with exothermic and endothermic reactions marked by arrows.](assets/ef09855e056c-50611-httpscdn-savemyexams-comuploads20250624433.png)

- **Step 2: **Applying Hess’ law, the lattice energy of KCl is:

  - **Δ*****H***<sub>***latt***</sub><sup>**θ**</sup>** = Δ*****H***<sub>***f***</sub><sup>**θ**</sup>** - **Δ*H*<sub>*1*</sub><sup>θ</sup>
  - Δ*H*<sub>*latt*</sub><sup>θ</sup> = Δ*H*<sub>*f*</sub><sup>θ</sup> - [(Δ*H*<sub>*at*</sub><sup>θ</sup> K) + (Δ*H*<sub>*at*</sub><sup>θ</sup> Cl) + (*IE*<sub>*1*</sub> K) + (*EA*<sub>*1*</sub> Cl)]
  - Step 3: Substitute in the numbers:
  - Δ*H*<sub>*latt*</sub><sup>θ</sup> = (-437) - [(+90) + (**+122) + (+418) + (-349)] = –718 kJ mol**<sup>**-1–1**</sup>

blocks.label: Worked Example
blocks.md:
Using the data below, calculate the Δ*H*<sub>*latt*</sub><sup>**θ **</sup>of magnesium oxide, MgO.

|   | **Δ*****H***<sub>***at***</sub><sup>**θ**</sup>** / kJ mol**<sup>**–1**</sup> | **IE**<sub>**1**</sub>** / EA**<sub>**1**</sub>** / kJ mol**<sup>**–1**</sup> | **IE**<sub>***2***</sub>** / EA**<sub>***2***</sub>** / kJ mol**<sup>**–1**</sup> |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mg | +148 | +736 | +1450 |
| O | +248 | –142 | +770 |
| **Δ*****H***<sub>***f***</sub><sup>**θ**</sup>** / kJ mol**<sup>**–1**</sup> |   |   |   |
| MgO | –602 |   |   |

**Answer:**

- **Step 1: **The corresponding Born-Haber cycle is:

![Born-Haber cycle diagram for magnesium oxide showing enthalpy changes: formation, atomisation, ionisation energies, electron affinities, and lattice enthalpy.](assets/524b02a135e9-46069-httpscdn-savemyexams-comuploads20250631408.png)

- **Step 2: **Applying Hess’ law, the lattice energy of MgO is:

  - **Δ*****H***<sub>***latt***</sub><sup>**θ**</sup><sub>*** ***</sub>** = Δ*****H***<sub>***f***</sub><sup>**θ**</sup><sub>*** ***</sub>** - Δ*****H***<sub>***1***</sub><sup>**θ**</sup>** **
  - **Δ*****H***<sub>***latt***</sub><sup>**θ **</sup>** = Δ*****H***<sub>***f***</sub><sup>**θ **</sup>** - [(Δ*****H***<sub>***at***</sub><sup>**θ **</sup>** Mg) + (Δ*****H***<sub>***at***</sub><sup>**θ **</sup>** O) + (IE**<sub>**1**</sub>** Mg) + (IE**<sub>***2***</sub>** Mg) + (EA**<sub>**1**</sub>** O) + (EA**<sub>***2***</sub>** O)]**
  - **Step 3: **Substitute in the numbers:
  - **Δ*****H***<sub>***latt***</sub><sup>**θ**</sup>** = (-602) - [(+148) + (+248) + (+736) + (+1450) + (-142) + (+770)]**

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: Make sure you use brackets when carrying out calculations using Born-Haber cycles as you may forget a +/- sign which will affect your final answer!
